description: Scan a local repository and return its architecture graph as JSON: one node per source file (id, layer, cluster, in/out degree, lines of code), import edges between files, nested directory clusters, and metrics (totalFiles, totalEdges, density, couplingFactor, deadCodeCount, foldedUtilityCount). Use it to understand how a codebase is organised, find hub files, or feed graph data into further analysis. Use query_impact_path instead when you only need the callers of one file, and generate_architecture_html when a human wants a visual map. Every call performs its own fresh static scan of `path`; no prior scan is required. Reads the local filesystem only, executes nothing, and sends nothing over the network. Supports TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go and Rust; external packages are dropped, test files are excluded, and layer labels (entry/business/data/util/unknown) are filename heuristics, not semantic judgements.

collapseUtils.description: Whether to mark high fan-in utility files (more than 15 callers and at most two dependencies, or utility-like names such as utils/helpers/types/config) as folded. Boolean, default true. Folded nodes stay in the graph data with isFolded: true; set false to treat every file equally.

maxDepth.description: Maximum directory nesting depth to scan below the root. Integer, default 6. Use 0 to scan only files in the root directory; raise it for deeply nested monorepos.

path.description: Absolute path to the repository root to scan, e.g. "/home/me/project" or "C:/dev/project". Relative paths resolve against the MCP server process working directory, which is usually not the project, so prefer absolute paths.

name: scan_repository_graph
title: Scan repository architecture graph
